# A fieldset's legend changes are lost when a sibling update makes the cycle sparse

## Context

#19402 (PR #19403, merged) fixed this class at `Component#hide()`. Its Out of Scope named three other owners that raise their own `updateDepth` before changing children, with no claim about them. At `dev` `05a161bb9f` each has the same shape: it changes children silently (`setSilent`), raises `updateDepth = 2` and leaves `denseUpdate` unset. Measuring found a red at one of them:
- **`form/Fieldset#updateLegend()`** (`src/form/Fieldset.mjs:211–242`): red, and this ticket's subject.
- **`tab/Container#afterSetTabBarPosition()`** (`src/tab/Container.mjs:250–267`): no red reachable today, excluded. The trace is under The Fix.
- **`calendar/view/calendars/List`** (`src/calendar/view/calendars/List.mjs:63–82`, the item builder): unmeasured, and no claim is made.

Fieldset also carries two defects of its own in the empty-legend branch, present since 2021 (`c1bbd220dc`):
- It writes `legend.vdom.reomveDom` (a typo, in both the set and the delete).
- It never raises the depth, so an emptied legend cannot leave the DOM even with the spelling fixed.

Red on `dev` (unit, two arms, `test/playwright/unit/form/FieldsetLegend.spec.mjs`):
- `title = ''` with `iconClsChecked: ''`: `legend.vdom.removeDom` stays `undefined` and no `removeNode` is emitted.
- Two renames in one pass, then a child's own update: no `updateVtext` reaches the legend's text node, and only the child's `textContent` (`Close`) is sent.

Sweeps at 2026-10-05T11:32Z:
- Live: the latest 20 open neo issues; none equivalent.
- Search: `reomveDom` and `fieldset legend`; no hits.
- A2A: my #19402 lane.
- MC: the 2026-01-20 sparse-tree design, read for #19402.
- Own: #19402 is the sibling; nothing else on this surface.

## The Problem

A fieldset's renamed legend keeps its old text, with no error, whenever a child's own update lands in the same cycle. An emptied legend never leaves the DOM at all.

## The Architectural Reality

- For `updateDepth !== 1` with merged children, `VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate` builds a sparse payload (`ids = mergedChildIds`). `TreeBuilder` prunes every other child to a `{componentId}` reference, on the reading that unmerged children are clean.
- `denseUpdate` is the documented exception, "the owner changed descendants silently within its `updateDepth`". `grid.View` sets it next to its depth bump, and #19403 adds it to `hide()`.
- `Fieldset#updateLegend()` changes its legend silently and does not set it.

## The Fix

**Fieldset `updateLegend()`:**
- Spell `removeDom` in both places.
- Raise `updateDepth = 2` in the empty branch too, so the removal is carried.
- Set `denseUpdate = true` wherever it raises the depth.

**Measured since filing, so no change at the other two sites:**
- **`tab/Container#afterSetTabBarPosition()` is not reachable.** Its own `me.setSilent({cls})` runs first and sets the container's `needsVdomUpdate`, so the bar's and the strip's silent updates register as merged children (traced: `container<-tab-header-toolbar`, `container<-tab-strip`) and are expanded. A card merging at distance 2 leaves the strip correct on `dev` and with the fix alike. The site is protected by that ordering, not by `denseUpdate`. A reorder would expose it, but no red exists today, so no line is added.
- **`calendar/view/calendars/List`** is unmeasured, and no claim is made.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The two Fieldset arms (`test/playwright/unit/form/FieldsetLegend.spec.mjs`), red on `dev` first: an emptied legend leaves the DOM, and a renamed legend's `updateVtext` is sent although a child's update merged into the cycle.
- [x] TabContainer: no red can be built. The reason is under The Fix.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` and `npm run test-components` stay green.

## Out of Scope

- `toolbar/Base` and the calendar `MainContainer` raise to depth −1, which `TreeBuilder` always builds dense, so they are not affected.
- Making `denseUpdate` implicit for every owner-raised depth is an engine design change and is not taken here.

## Related

- #19402 / PR #19403, the same class at `hide()`.
